Source-backed analysis of every layer in Frontier_Hacks: six-agent pipeline, providers, tools, Streamlit UI, evaluation, and the gap between design docs and the code that actually runs. What the product is

WorthApply is a student-facing opportunity intelligence system. Input is a resume (PDF/DOCX/TXT) plus a job URL or pasted description. Output is an Opportunity Intelligence Report: student fit with resume evidence, company/posting verification, risk signals, evidence quality, and a recommendation of APPLY / APPLY IF TIME / LOW PRIORITY. The stated bottleneck is investigation time — 15–45 minutes per posting, 10–30 postings per week. The system is decision support only: it does not apply, contact recruiters, or treat risk signals as proof of fraud.

Repository map

Stack

Runtime Python 3.11+, Pydantic v2, OpenAI-compatible client, httpx, trafilatura/BeautifulSoup, PyPDF2, python-docx, Streamlit, pytest. Config LLM_PROVIDER=xai|local, XAI_API_KEY, XAI_MODEL (default grok-3-mini-fast), SERPER_API_KEY (optional), LOCAL_MODEL / LOCAL_BASE_URL, BATCH_CONCURRENCY, CASE_PAUSE_SECONDS.

Design principle vs measured behavior

The architecture’s core claim is dimension separation: a student can be a 95% fit for a HIGH-risk posting, and both facts must stay visible. Agents and schemas honor that. Decision synthesis and the Category A eval run do not — HIGH risk + failed verification overrode strong fit into LOW priority.
Target metrics from PROJECT_PLAN.md: ≥80% decision accuracy, ≥75% fit, ≥70% evidence support, ≥70% risk detection, <60s latency, <$0.10/case. Measured pipeline: 56% exact / 72% weighted, 36% fit, 48% risk, ~299s/case, $0 (local run).

Actual run order

README and architecture.md draw Company Verification and Student Fit as parallel. AnalysisWorkflow awaits them one after the other because free-tier TPM (~8k tokens/min) 429s on two structured calls at once.
Every stage is try/except’d. A failed agent does not abort the run — later stages receive empty defaults. That is why Category A still produced a full report instead of crashing when web verification found nothing.

State and tracing

PipelineState holds inputs, intermediate models, evidence_quality, unsupported_claims, the final OpportunityReport, per-stage StageResult (PENDING/RUNNING/COMPLETED/FAILED/SKIPPED), and token usage. run_id is a 12-char UUID. Tracer writes one JSON file per agent under traces/<case_or_run_id>/. Tool-call logging exists on Tracer but agents do not call log_tool_call, so traces are input/output summaries plus usage — not the actual Serper/DDG queries.

Agent-by-agent

Every agent extends BaseAgent: 3 retries, Groq/OpenAI 429 wait parsing, and a 1024-token cap when provider_name == local. Extracts JobProfile from up to 6000 chars of posting text. Prompt forbids invented company/title/date/skills. Post-LLM sanitizer drops placeholder companies (Acme, XYZ Technologies), ungrounded posting_date, invented education requirements, and a specific false-positive: bare “AWS” when the JD only mentions Amazon Bedrock as an example. Fallback heuristics: first line containing engineer/developer/ intern… as title; “Company:” / “Employer:” as company. LLM produces StudentFitResult, then deterministic grounding rewrites it. Required/preferred lists are atomized (split on commas / parentheses). Each skill is MATCHED / PARTIALLY_MATCHED / MISSING via resume substring + 13 concept families (python, ml, dl, genai, cloud, devops…) and nearby-family transfer (AWS↔Azure, PyTorch↔TensorFlow). Fit score is blended: 35% LLM + 65% grounded (matched + 0.55×partial) / required. Then apply_experience_gate parses JD min years vs resume date ranges / internships and hard-caps score (18–38) when the gap is large. sanitize_fit_narratives drops false AWS gaps and “education in a different field” for IT/CS students on software roles. Multi-signal pack: fetch applicant URL, up to 6 targeted searches (official site, about, LinkedIn, careers, title+company), then fetch up to 3 non-board pages. Job-board hosts (Indeed, Naukri, Greenhouse, Internshala…) are treated as normal listing channels — a board URL must not set job_listing_found. Heuristics can promote UNVERIFIED → PARTIALLY_VERIFIED / VERIFIED when name_hits and website/careers flags agree. On the 25-case eval this layer systematically failed: synthetic company names have no real web footprint, so verification stayed empty and downstream risk went HIGH. Looks at posting content first (pay-to-apply, telegram-only, missing details), then company identity. Job-board-only “unverified site” notes are downgraded to LOW. If the company is VERIFIED / PARTIALLY_VERIFIED or website_found, HIGH is capped to LOW. That cap did not fire on Category A because website_found was false. The agent then treated “cannot retrieve careers page” as a serious signal — the opposite of the prompt’s “missing official listing alone ⇒ at most LOW”. extract_claims() splits fit/risk/verification summaries on sentences and keeps those with keywords (match, skill, risk, company…). Max 15 claims. LLM labels each SUPPORTED / UNSUPPORTED / CONFLICTING and returns overall_evidence_quality plus unsupported_count. The result is only two strings/ints on PipelineState. It does not rewrite other agents’ claims. models/evidence.py (Claim, EvidenceStore) is the designed evidence layer — it is imported only in tests, never in the workflow. Prompt explicitly says keep fit / confidence / risk / evidence separate, and APPLY requires strong fit AND confident opportunity AND low risk. Output is SynthesisOutput, then mapped onto OpportunityReport. Gap lists are re-sanitized (AWS / education-field filters) and uncertainty is de-duped against concerns. Rule 5 in the system prompt is the collapse: HIGH risk or failed verification forces LOW_PRIORITY even at 80 fit. models/schemas.py is the contract. Enums: SkillMatchLevel, VerificationStatus (5 values), RiskLevel, Recommendation, Priority. WorthApply ek **6-agent opportunity-intelligence system** hai: resume + job posting se fit, company verification, risk, evidence quality, aur APPLY / APPLY IF TIME / LOW PRIORITY alag-alag dimensions mein nikalta hai. Design strong hai; measured happy-path abhi toot raha hai.

Poora breakdown ek interactive review mein hai — [WorthApply architecture review](C:\Users\kamal\.cursor\projects\c-Users-kamal-Desktop-Frontier-Hacks\canvases\worthapply-architecture-review.canvas.tsx). Yeh ek Canvas hai: chat ke side mein open karke Overview, Pipeline, Agents, Layers, Evaluation, Findings tabs switch kar sakte ho. Tables aur charts ke liye yeh text dump se better hai.

---

## Product kya karta hai

Student ka resume (PDF/DOCX/TXT) + job URL ya pasted JD. Output: **Opportunity Intelligence Report** — skill match with resume evidence, company/posting verification, risk signals (accusation nahi), evidence quality, recommendation.

Core rule: fit aur risk mix nahi hone chahiye. 95% fit + HIGH risk dono dikhne chahiye. Schemas isko follow karte hain; Category A eval run nahi karta.

---

## Har layer, short

| Layer | Kya hai | Actual behavior |
|---|---|---|
| **Job Intelligence** | JD → `JobProfile` | Placeholder company/title/date drop; Bedrock-example se fake AWS skill nahi |
| **Student Fit** | Resume vs required/preferred | LLM + concept-family grounding (AWS↔Azure); experience-years hard cap (7+ JD vs intern → score ~18–38) |
| **Company Verification** | Search + page fetch | Job boards (Indeed/Naukri) normal channel; official site alag. Synthetic eval companies yahan fail |
| **Opportunity Risk** | Signals, not fraud | Board-only “unverified” ko LOW karna chahiye; Category A par HIGH ho gaya |
| **Evidence Verifier** | Claim audit | Summaries se sentences nikalta hai; result sirf quality string. `EvidenceStore` design hai, pipeline use nahi karti |
| **Decision Synthesizer** | Final rec + priority | Prompt kehta hai dimensions alag rakho, phir HIGH risk par LOW_PRIORITY force karta hai |

**Providers:** `LLMProvider` ABC → xAI/Grok ya Ollama. Agents vendor SDK nahi chhoote.

**Tools:** resume parse, Serper (warna DuckDuckGo HTML), `httpx` + trafilatura fetch. JS career pages often empty.

**UI:** Streamlit — single analyze, batch (2–10 jobs, `BATCH_CONCURRENCY`), live stages, history (50 reports), markdown/JSON download.

**Orchestration:** Docs mein Company Verify + Fit parallel hain. Code sequential hai (free-tier TPM / 429s). Har stage fail hone par stub ke saath aage badhta hai.

---

## Evaluation — sabse important number

`results/final/` par 25/25 cases complete hue (~5 min/case, local run, $0):

- Exact priority: **56%** (target ≥80%)
- Weighted: **72%**
- Recommendation: **78%**
- Fit: **36%**
- Risk: **48%**

**Category A (legitimate + strong fit) = 0.0.** Teenon cases expected HIGH/APPLY the; system ne LOW/LOW_PRIORITY diya. Reason chain:

1. Synthetic company ka real website nahi  
2. Verification fail  
3. Risk → HIGH  
4. Synthesizer ne 60–80 fit ignore karke LOW_PRIORITY de diya  

Category B/G (weak fit) 1.0 score — sahi LOW, lekin zyada tar galat reason se (risk, fit nahi). Baseline 88% dikhta hai lekin 8/25 timeout; Category A isliye pass hua kyunki single prompt web search karta hi nahi. Fair comparison abhi missing hai.

---

## Jo design mein hai, code mein nahi

- `models/evidence.py` (`EvidenceStore`) sirf tests mein import  
- `docs/architecture.md` abhi bhi kehta hai “only baseline implemented”  
- Changelog / README: “NOT YET EVALUATED” — results already exist  
- UI progress text hardcode: “Using local Ollama”  
- Privacy doc: resume store nahi; `history.json` full report store karta hai  

---

## Highest-leverage fixes

1. Verification fail ko HIGH risk / LOW priority mat banao jab sirf signal “no public website” ho — `APPLY_IF_TIME` + low confidence.  
2. Eval set ko verification oracle do, ya synthetic names par live search skip karo.  
3. `EvidenceStore` wire karo ya hatao.  
4. Baseline 25 cases par dubara chalao, changelog update karo — yahi experiment `docs/hot_take.md` promise karta hai.

Canvas mein har agent ke prompts/heuristics, file inventory, aur category-wise chart hai. Kisi ek part (fit gate, verification heuristics, ya UI report) ko next deep-dive chahiye to batao.

- **1–15:** ~70–80s / case — normal (chal raha tha)

- Case 17–20: **3.5–6 min** each, mostly waiting, not generating

Baseline tez tha kyunki **1 LLM call**. Final pipeline **6 sequential agents** + web search + page fetch. Comment in code: free-tier TPM (~8k/min) do badi calls ek saath nahi sambhalti, isliye parallel bhi nahi.

| Kahan time jata hai | Kyun |
|---|---|
| 6 LLM calls, ek ke baad ek | Job Intel → Company Verify → Fit → Risk → Evidence → Decision |
| ~6 DuckDuckGo searches / case | Local `.env` mein Serper nahi; har search 1–12s |
| Groq 429 after ~16 cases | Free/dev RPM–TPM khatam; 6 agents × 3 retries × 16s = **~5 extra min / case** |
| 6s pause cases ke beech | Extra; ab bottleneck 429 wait hai |

Isliye live app “fast” lagti hai (1 job), yeh run nahi — **25 × 6 calls** same Groq key pe.

Chalne do: 20/25 save ho chuke hain (`raw_results.json`). Last 5 agar 429 pe rahe to ~20–30 min aur. Stop mat karna — progress waste ho jayegi.
